about.headline: WHO ARE THE OREGON DUCKS
copy: Chip Kelly, 2009 to 2012. {record|46 and 7}. The most feared offense in college football.
Spread them out. Snap it every 19 seconds. Run it {rushyd|315 yards a game} right down their throat.

principles.title: SPREAD TO RUN
principles.blurb: Spread the field sideline to sideline, then run through the space it creates.
principles.detail: Four and five wide is not a passing look here, it is a run formation. Spreading the field forces the defense to match personnel, and the second they do the box empties out. With the quarterback as a live run threat, the offense always has one more runner than the defense has defenders.

principles.title: MAKE DEFENSES WRONG
principles.blurb: Put a defender in a bind on every snap, wrong no matter what he does.
principles.detail: Every play forces a defender into conflict. Crash the run and the ball goes over his head. Drop for the pass and it gets handed off downhill. There is no guessing on offense, just a read that takes whatever the defense gives up.

principles.title: STRESS THE FIELD
principles.blurb: Make the defense cover every blade of grass, then take the opening.
principles.detail: All that horizontal spacing is what unlocks the pass. Spreading the defense out opens huge throwing windows and one-on-one matchups on the outside, so once the front collapses to stop the run, the shot goes up over the top into the space it left behind.

stats.label: RECORD
stats.note: Two BCS bowls and a national title game in four seasons.

stats.label: POINTS / GAME
stats.note: Led the nation in scoring in 2010. Climbing every season.

stats.label: PLAYS / GAME
stats.note: A snap every 19 seconds. The pace never stopped rising.

stats.label: RUSH YDS / GAME
stats.note: Top three in the nation on the ground every season.

stats.label: YARDS / CARRY
stats.note: Every carry moved half the sticks.

stats.label: HOME WIN STREAK
stats.note: Autzen was a fortress. Twenty three straight at home.

extras.text: We want to play fast. Faster than anyone in the country.

jobs: SPEED TO MAKE PLAYS ON THE EDGE.
READS THE END AND NEVER GUESSES WRONG.
DELIVERS STRIKES ON THE QUICK GAME.
TURNS ROUTINE TOUCHES INTO EXPLOSIVE GAINS.
A REAL THREAT OUT OF THE BACKFIELD.

TILTS COVERAGE JUST BY BEING ON THE FIELD.

lineage.name: MARCUS MARIOTA
stats: 42 total TD in the Heisman year
lineage.brought: The cleanest zone read trigger the scheme ever produced. Every wrong step a defense took turned into a chunk play the other way. Calm, fast, and never fooled twice by the same look.

lineage.name: PAT WHITE
stats: Won four straight bowls as the starter
lineage.brought: The original dual threat. Defenses knew the read was coming for four straight years and still could not stop it. Nobody punished a crashing end harder, and nobody made the option look easier.

lineage.name: LAMICHAEL JAMES
lineage.brought: The engine of the blur. One cut, zero wasted steps, and the scoreboard moved. Back to back seasons over 1,700 yards because the offense never let a defense set its feet.

lineage.name: TREVEYON HENDERSON
stats: 75 yd TD to ice the title game
lineage.brought: Home run speed that closed out a championship. Never needed volume, only a crease, and the 75 yarder against Texas is the proof. The best pass protecting back in the sport on top of it.

lineage.name: DE'ANTHONY THOMAS
stats: 1,890 all purpose yds as a sophomore
lineage.brought: The Black Mamba. Lined up everywhere and scored from everywhere. Space around him was a death sentence, so every defense had to find him before the snap and most of them still lost him.

lineage.name: TAVON AUSTIN
stats: 572 total yds in one game vs Oklahoma
lineage.brought: The jet motion nightmare no defense ever solved. Every yard started with the defense leaning the wrong way, and the Oklahoma tape is still the scariest game a slot has ever put out.

lineage.name: JEREMIAH SMITH
lineage.brought: The standard. Won at the catch point every single time as a true freshman on a title team, and tilted coverage just by walking on the field. Safeties rolled his way all year and it did not matter.

lineage.name: JOSH HUFF
lineage.brought: Play action cashed its checks outside for four straight years. The blur held the safeties in the box, and Huff made them pay over the top every time they cheated.

formations.name: Wing Trio Wk
formations.desc: A trips look to the wide side of the field with a wing tucked to the formation. It carries the whole offense - the buck sweep and RPO run game, the auto-rollout pass game, and the play-action floods that punish a defense keying the run.
bullets: Trips to the wide side with a wing to the formation
Downhill run game with multiple pullers
Auto-rollout pass game for a mobile QB
Play-action floods off the run look

formations.name: Split Slot Open
formations.desc: An open spread set with the slot to the wide side. This is the heart of the RPO run game - the peek swing and triple option get the box light, and once they load it up the play-action verticals take the top off.
bullets: Slot to the wide side of the field
RPO run game gets the box light
Triple option threatens all three levels
Play-action verticals off the run action

formations.name: Gun Double Stack
formations.desc: An empty, triple-stack look that forces the defense to defend the whole field. The stacks create natural picks and free releases - if they don't match it the bubble is free, and if they empty the box the QB draw takes off.
bullets: Empty triple-stack look, five eligible threats
Stacks create picks and clean releases
Bubble and smoke screens built in
QB draw when the box empties out

formations.name: Empty Base
formations.desc: A five-wide empty set with trips to one side. It gets every skill player into a route, spaces the defense out, and gives quick, reliable answers versus man, zone, and any overplay.

Stick and flood concepts vs any coverage
Quick answers versus man and zone

title.name: THE SPREAD TO RUN OFFENSE
title.sub: One system. Three programs. A thousand miles apart, running the same play.

teams.name: OREGON
teams.writeup: The blur years. Chip Kelly took the spread run game and strapped a jet engine to it: no huddle, no mercy. From 2009 to 2012 Oregon went 46 and 7, played for a national title, and won four straight BCS bowls out of Eugene. LaMichael James ran for over 1,700 twice while the Ducks led the country in scoring, snapping the ball before defenses could even get lined up.

teams.name: OHIO STATE
teams.writeup: The proof it still wins. Chip Kelly came back to call the plays, the spread run game set the table, and Ohio State ran through the entire sport in 2024: a national championship behind a true freshman phenom in Jeremiah Smith. Twenty years after Morgantown, the same offense is still carving defenses apart.
teams.lockMsg: FULL BREAKDOWN DROPS WITH THE SCHEME

teams.name: WEST VIRGINIA
teams.writeup: The birthplace. Rich Rodriguez drew the modern zone read up in Morgantown and handed it to two blurs. In 2006 alone Pat White and Steve Slaton piled up 2,963 rushing yards together, and White walked away as the only quarterback in history to start and win four bowl games. Every zone read defenses chase on Saturdays traces back to here.

pillars.name: The Base
pillars.line: The plays the whole offense is built on, the ones you come back to when nothing else is working.

pillars.name: The Expansion

plays.name: MTN RPO Peek Swing

reads.label: RB on the Perimeter (First Look)
reads.text: First look is the running back going out on the perimeter with two blockers in front of him. If you've got a numbers advantage out there, fire it out to him right away and let him make plays in space.

reads.label: Hand It Off Downhill
reads.text: If once you snap it you see the user, the linebackers, or extra defenders leave the box to chase that back on the perimeter, that opens up the middle of the field. Hand it off to your other back, get downhill, and there should be a ton of green grass to work with in the middle.

reads.label: Backside Slant
reads.text: If the linebackers are biting down on the back in the middle, the slant is breaking in right behind them. That's your third option - throw it in over the top of them.

adjustments: Slot receiver to the wide side of the field.
Swing to the perimeter with two blockers out front.
plays.whenToUse: This is the Oregon run game in one call - spread spacing plus a read that keeps the box light. Come out in split slot open with your slot to the wide side. If they give you numbers out there, take the swing. If they leave the box to chase it, hand it off downhill. And if the linebackers crash the middle, the slant is sitting right behind them.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__MTN RPO Peek Swing Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Triple Option LT

reads.label: Read 1: Defensive End Crashes
reads.text: If the DE crashes hard, pull the ball and keep it with the QB or get to the pitch. The crash opens up the perimeter for the pitch man.

reads.label: Read 2: DE Plays QB / Edge Overloaded
reads.text: If the DE plays the QB and overloads the outside, hand the ball off downhill to the running back for easy yardage.

reads.label: Read 3: Multiple Defenders Drawn In
reads.text: If defenders swarm toward the QB and the pitch man is drawing coverage, use the QB to suck defenders in, then flip the pitch out to the perimeter for a one-on-one on the edge.

reads.label: Read 4: One-on-One on the Edge
reads.text: Once the pitch is made and you have a single defender on the edge, attack the angle - the pitch man should win that matchup and score or gain big.

adjustments: DE crashes - keep or pitch.
DE plays the edge - give the ball.
Defenders drawn in - pitch it out.
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you've got an athletic QB who can threaten all three options. It's a Swiss Army knife - red zone, goal line, anywhere on the field. The defense has to be right on all three reads or somebody's getting a walk-in score.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__Triple Option LT Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Buck Sweep

reads.label: Follow the Pullers
reads.text: This is a downhill run with multiple pullers getting out in front of your playmaking back. Follow those guys right through the hole. Once they blow the defenders off the football, get downhill, put your foot in the ground, and be explosive.

reads.label: Foot in the Ground
reads.text: When the pullers wall it off, put your foot in the ground and go. Don't dance - this play is at its best when you hit it north and south and let your back's speed take over.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field.
Multiple pullers leading through the hole.
plays.whenToUse: This is your downhill hammer. It's at its best once you've built up the deep passing game and they're respecting it - now you drop the hammer, go right back to the run game, and just bludgeon them with this one. When they're playing soft over the top, put your foot in the ground and get physical yards.

plays.name: QB Draw

reads.label: Defender Count in the Box
reads.text: Count defenders in the box. If the defense spreads out to match your empty receivers, they leave only 4 defenders in the middle against your 5 OL - that's your green light to pull the trigger on the draw.

reads.label: Safety Positioning
reads.text: If both safeties are playing deep or wide to defend the pass, the middle of the field opens up. That's your lane - take it with the QB draw.

reads.label: Wide Side Overload
reads.text: If the defense sends extra defenders to the wide side to account for trips, they're thinning out the box. Count it up - 5 blockers vs. 4 in the box means you go.

adjustments: QB draw in the audible package.
Receivers block downfield.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you're in empty and the defense spreads out to match your receivers. They're playing your pass - make them pay. Five blockers against four in the box, your QB is basically untouched through the hole. Works anywhere on the field, but it's a killer in the red zone.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__QB Draw Screen Shot Empty Base.webp

plays.name: Empty Bubble Screen

reads.label: They Don't Match the Trips Stack
reads.text: If they don't match that three-stack look to the wide side, throw the bubble out to your back-stacked player. He's got two blockers out in front of him, and there are a ton of easy yards waiting on the wide side of the field.

reads.label: They Cheat the Short-Side Stack
reads.text: If they stay spread to the triple stack but cheat inside on the normal stack to the short side, you've got a quick smoke screen right there with a blocker. Flip it out that way instead.

reads.label: They Spread Out to Match Everything
reads.text: If they spread everybody out to match all your looks on the outside, now you've got nobody left in the box. Turn this into a QB draw - with five wide in these stack looks, there's a ton of running room for your quarterback to take off up the field and rip off a big play.

adjustments: Triple stack to the wide side of the field.
Bubble to the back-stacked player.
QB draw built in when the box empties.
plays.whenToUse: This is the perfect first install because however they line up, you've got the answer. Don't match the stack and the bubble is free. Cheat the short side and the smoke is open the other way. Spread out to cover it all and you run the QB draw into an empty box. Come out in empty, force them to defend the whole field, and take what the defense gives you.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__Empty Bubble Screen  Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Y Cross Flood

reads.label: Wide-Side Slot Option (Go-To)
reads.text: The go-to route is the wide-side slot on an option route. Against zone he sits down, so if everybody's playing back, drop it into his hitch and let him make plays after the catch. Against man he's got a one-on-one, breaks to the outside, and usually gets really good separation.

reads.label: Crosser From the Trips Side
reads.text: If it's zone but defenders are biting down on that hitch and playing shallow, come to the crosser from the trips side. If the linebackers bite down, throw it in over their heads in the middle. Or wait for him to keep crossing all the way over, get in behind the flat defender on the wide side, and drop it in behind him.

reads.label: Post-Sit on the Trips Side
reads.text: If the linebackers get pulled inside by the crossing route and the short-side flat defender bites down on the out, the post-sit on the trips side is just sitting there open against zone. A great third option.

reads.label: Out Route (Short-Side Middle)
reads.text: The out route from the middle receiver on the short side is a good option against zone when everybody's playing off - just check it down to him. It can also be a good option against man.

adjustments: Trips to the short side of the field.
Outside trips receiver on a post-sit route.
Wide-side slot on the option route.
plays.whenToUse: Everything this offense is built on feeds right into this play - spread them out, make them wrong, stress the field. Come out with trips to the short side and let the wide-side option route carry it. Against zone he sits, against man he breaks it off for separation. When they take that away, the crosser and post-sit open up underneath and behind them.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__Y Cross Flood Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Dash X Hitch

reads.label: Deep Corner Route (Go-To)
reads.text: This play starts with an auto-rollout out of the backfield with your quarterback. The go-to is the super deep corner route that gets about thirty yards down the field, in behind the zones. With an athletic quarterback out on the edge, just drop this in for huge gains.

reads.label: RB Checkdown on the Perimeter
reads.text: Once you're out on the edge, if they're playing way back and taking that corner route away, check it down to the running back who's already out on the perimeter in front of you. Drop it into him and let him make plays in the open field.

reads.label: Shallow Cross
reads.text: If the linebackers leave the middle to try to take away the back in the flat or the corner route deep, the shallow cross is breaking into the middle of the field. Fire that one in.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field.
Backside solo receiver on a shallow cross.
Outside wide-side receiver stemmed deeper on the post.
plays.whenToUse: This is a play all three spread-to-run eras could've run with their mobile, athletic quarterbacks. The auto-rollout puts your QB on the edge with a deep corner over the top and a checkdown underneath. It's a great third-down answer to keep a drive alive - branch it off as your fallback for when you get stalled out.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__Dash X Hitch Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Empty Fake Bubble Post

reads.label: Wheel on the Triple-Stack Side (Go-To)
reads.text: The go-to route is the wheel on the triple-stack side. There's a glitch in the coverage where once you snap the ball, everybody jumps forward on the fake screen look, and that wheel gets open super, super consistently. I've thrown this for thirty and forty-yard bombs down the field.

reads.label: Shallow Cross
reads.text: Coming underneath you've got the shallow cross. If that wheel ever does get covered, this is a clean answer working across the middle of the field.

reads.label: Deep Post From the Triple Stack
reads.text: The deeper post from the triple-stack receiver is your other answer over the top. If they take the wheel away, work back to the post breaking into the middle of the field.

adjustments: Triple-stack side receivers to the wide side of the field.
Short-side front-of-stack player on a wheel.
plays.whenToUse: This is one of the best man beaters I've used all year. Come out with the triple stack to the wide side and put the short-side front-of-stack player on the wheel. The fake screen look freezes everybody, the wheel comes wide open, and if it's ever covered you've got the shallow cross and the deep post right off of it.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__Empty FK Bubble Post screen shot.webp

images.playCall: art/Oregon Assets__Empty FK Bubble Post Play.webp

plays.name: Dig Curl Read

reads.label: Inside Slot Skinny Post (Key Route)
reads.text: The key route is the inside slot on the skinny post - it gets to a nasty area of the field. Against Cover 3 this can be a one-play touchdown: let him clear the middle safety, the corner route holds the backside corner down, and bomb him over the top. Against Cover 2 you split the two high safeties, and if the linebackers stay shallow it's a money shot right down the middle of the field.

reads.label: Whip Underneath (Checkdown)
reads.text: The whip underneath is your checkdown. If the deep shot isn't there, take the easy completion underneath and keep the drive on schedule.

reads.label: Dig Over the Middle
reads.text: If everybody's playing way back, the dig breaks back in over the middle of the field. Work to it when the defense bails and takes the post away deep.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field.
Middle trips receiver on a streak.
Short-side outside receiver on a corner route.
plays.whenToUse: This is the shot play built right into the offense. Come out with trips to the wide side and let that inside-slot skinny post go to work. Any time you get a Cover 3 or Cover 2 look where you know you can take your deep shot, this is your counter - branch it off and pull the trigger.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__Dig Curl Read Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Motion Z Cross

reads.label: Primary: Motion Crosser
reads.text: The auto-motion crossing route is the money route. It is unbumpable against press coverage and generates four to ten-plus yards of separation as it comes across the field. Fire it in on time.

reads.label: Secondary: RB Out Route
reads.text: If the user bites on the crosser and abandons the running back, the RB will be wide open in the flat. The linebacker in man often thinks the RB is blocking and vacates, leaving a walk-in score.

reads.label: Third: Backside Solo Post
reads.text: If the user chases the deep crosser and leaves the middle, the solo receiver's post breaks the opposite way for a big gain. Look here when the user over-commits to the drag.

reads.label: Fourth: Dig (Late Read)
reads.text: The inside slot's dig breaks in behind the crosser in the middle of the field. If the defense is occupied by the three primary routes, the dig can come open as a clean underneath option.

adjustments: Inside slot on a corner route.
Trips to the wide side of the field.
RB on an out route.
Solo receiver on a backside post.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when they're living in man coverage. It doesn't matter if they're pressing - the motion crosser is unbumpable and gets automatic separation. Six-man protection gives you time to let it develop. This is your go-to man beater.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__MTN Z Cross Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: PA Verts

reads.label: Wide Side Seam
reads.text: Primary read off the play-action fake. If the linebacker bites downhill on the run fake and the safety is pulled down, attack the wide-side seam with the slot receiver over the top.

reads.label: Weak Side Seam (RB)
reads.text: If the wide-side seam is covered, work to the running back releasing up the weak-side seam. Comebacks will widen the corners and create room for this throw.

reads.label: Comebacks (Both Sides)
reads.text: Against man or Cover 3 match coverage where the seams get taken away, work to the comeback routes on either side. Flat defenders playing shallow leave the comeback open underneath - throw it on the break.

reads.label: RB Checkdown (Zone Bail)
reads.text: If everyone vertically is matched and defenders are riding routes down the field, dump it down to the running back sitting in the vacated zone after the play fake.

adjustments: Slot receiver to the wide side.
plays.whenToUse: No setup needed - run it stock. This is your go-to shot against Cover 3 when you've been pounding the ball out of split slot. The more you run out of this formation, the more that linebacker is going to fly downhill on the fake. That's when you take the top off.

plays.name: 689 Hook

reads.label: 1st Read - Deep Z Post (vs. Cover 3)
reads.text: Single high safety look. As the deep post clears the middle safety, let it fly over the top for the touchdown.

reads.label: 2nd Read - Deep Z Post (vs. Cover 2)
reads.text: Watch the mid-read linebacker. If he stops his feet and doesn't ride the post all the way down the field, the window opens over the top - bomb it.

reads.label: 3rd Read - RB Checkdown
reads.text: Under pressure or if the deep shots are taken away, the running back sits down in the flat. Dump it off and live to play the next down.

adjustments: RB on a wide-side streak.
Backside X on an out route.
RB sits in the flat on pressure.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you need a walk-in touchdown against single high or split safeties. Cover 3 is the ideal look - the post clears the safety and it's over. Cover 2 works too as long as that mid linebacker doesn't ride it deep. Great shot play any time you want to take the top off the defense.

plays.name: Empty Bubble Spot Out

reads.label: Corner Route vs Flat Defender
reads.text: Watch the flat defender's depth. If he stays shallow at 10-15 yards instead of getting to 20-25, drop the corner route in over his head behind him.

reads.label: Streak/Fade Holding Deep Defenders
reads.text: The streak/fade on the wide side pulls deep defenders back. Use this to create the window for the corner route underneath.

reads.label: Mesh Drags vs Man
reads.text: Against man coverage, fire to whichever drag has more separation as they cross. Defenders may run into each other, creating a clean window.

reads.label: Dig vs Zone (Hooks Biting Down)
reads.text: Against zone, if hook or flat defenders bite down on the crossing drags, the dig coming in behind them opens up the middle of the field. Layer it in over their heads.

adjustments: Middle stack player on a streak.
Backside stack player on a drag.
Short-side receiver on a drag.
Dig over the top of the mesh.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you want to stress the whole field out of one look. The stack gives you natural pick potential in the mesh, the corner route punishes any flat defender playing too shallow, and the dig is your answer when zone defenders start chasing the drags. Run it when you need a play that works vs man and zone without changing a thing.
plays.heroShot: art/Oregon Assets__Empty Bubble Spot Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: All Go

reads.label: Cover 3 - Seam
reads.text: Read the flat defender. If he widens and the wheel pulls the deep defender out, fire the wide-side seam up the middle. If the single-high safety is late rotating from the opposite side, this can be a touchdown.

reads.label: Cover 3 - Post
reads.text: If the seam is taken away or you don't like the look, let the play develop. The safety will bite on the seam, opening the post breaking over the middle. Look seam first, then pull the trigger on the post.

reads.label: Cover 2 - Post/Seam
reads.text: If the mid-read linebacker doesn't defend deep enough or is absent, the backside wheel pulls the deep-half safety, and the seam bends into a post over the top. Bomb them over the safety inside the 5.

reads.label: Cover 2 - Wheel (Hole Shot)
reads.text: Once the wheel gets outside the flat defender on the wide side, drop the hole shot in front of the safety, who is held by the streak coming right at him. If all deep shots are covered, check down to the RB on the option route.

adjustments: RB to the wide side.
Front stack receiver on a post.
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you want to attack two-high and three-deep zones with one concept. The wheel and seam stress every level of the defense at once. Set it up with your run game first, then drop this on them when they start loading the box. It's your go-to deep shot - not a man coverage play, but if you're in man, go post or check down to the RB.

plays.name: Stick

reads.label: 1. Stick Route (TE)
reads.text: Primary read. Against man, the TE breaks to the outside and you fire into the separation - four to five yards, easy first down. Against zone, the TE sits down in the soft spot; a linebacker playing back means you get the ball out quick for four to six yards.

reads.label: 2. Slot Out Route (Trips Side)
reads.text: Against off-zone with the flat dropping back, throw the out route as the slot breaks. Against man, wait for separation as the defender trails, then fire it in.

reads.label: 3. Comeback (Outside Trips Receiver)
reads.text: Against hard flat zone, the flat defender gets pulled down by the out route - throw the comeback into the vacated space as the deep defender drops off. Against man, comebacks are highly effective; fire in when he breaks back to the football with the flat defender playing shallow.

reads.label: 4. Backside Slants (Backside Adjustment)
reads.text: If the defense overplays the trips side at the snap - the user jumps to that side, linebackers cheat - flip your eyes to the backside. Look to the shallow slant first, then the deeper slant behind it. Against zone, find the hole; against man, take whichever is more open.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
Middle slot on an out route.
Outside trips receiver on a comeback.
Backside shallow and deep slants.
plays.whenToUse: Run this on third down when you need a quick, reliable answer versus any coverage. Empty gets you five eligible threats and stick gives you a built-in answer for man, zone, and overplays. Especially nasty in the red zone when linebackers cheat to the trips side - the backside slants will eat them alive.

plays.name: RPO Alert Slant

reads.label: Linebackers Stay Back
reads.text: If linebackers are getting depth and safeties are staying back, hand the ball off and let the pulling guard lead through the hole. This is the default read - lean toward the run.

reads.label: Linebackers Step Down or Crash Inside
reads.text: If either linebacker steps down or crashes inside, your eyes go backside. The slant is working right into that vacated hole. Fire it in behind them - especially lethal in the red zone.

reads.label: Off Coverage on the Perimeter
reads.text: If the corner is backed off and the apex or flat defender is staying inside committed to the run, you have a one-on-one block outside. Take the quick screen and let your receiver work upfield.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side.
Pulling guard leads the run.
Backside slant vs. crashing linebackers.
Quick screen vs. off coverage.
plays.whenToUse: This is a Swiss Army knife RPO - run it when you need answers. I lean run unless those linebackers show me something. Red zone especially, the backside slant is automatic when they crash. If they give you off coverage on the perimeter, take the screen and get your playmaker in space.

plays.name: PA Y Flood

reads.label: TE Corner Route (Go-To)
reads.text: This starts with a play-action fake to pull defenders down into the box. The go-to route is the corner route from the tight end - he gets in behind the flat defenders unless they're playing way back, and you drop this in for big pickups. It's also a really good option against man or match: he'll break it off, get really good separation, and you fire it in.

reads.label: Slot Post vs Cover 3 (One-Play TD)
reads.text: Against Cover 3 this is a one-play touchdown down the middle. The corner route pulls the deep defender back, the backside outside post keeps that middle safety in the middle of the field, and the post from your slot receiver gets up over the top. Drop that in for six.

reads.label: Backside Solo Corner vs Man
reads.text: If you're ever facing man, the corner route on the backside solo side is a really good answer. Work to it when they lock up outside.

reads.label: RB Checkdown
reads.text: If everything's covered up deep, just drop it into your running back underneath and let him make people miss in the open field.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field.
Backside solo receiver on a corner route.
Outside trips receiver stemmed down a notch on the post.
plays.whenToUse: This is a star play because it answers whatever the defense gives you. The play-action fake pulls defenders down, the tight end corner beats zone and man, and against Cover 3 the slot post over the top is a one-play touchdown. When everything's covered, the checkdown keeps it on schedule. Tag it and lean on it when you need a play that does it all.
